verdict.rationale: FireHydrant documents a general API that can do "anything you can do on the FireHydrant UI". It also has token-based API keys and bot tokens for non-human callers, plus an official MCP server for interacting with its API. Together these make a dashboard-free agent loop plausible, but no evidence shows the specific acknowledge, escalate and resolve operations end to end. Missing for 10: documented endpoints or MCP tools for acknowledging alerts, escalating via policies and resolving incidents; hands-on corroboration of an agent running the full lifecycle.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, my agent can acknowledge, escalate, and resolve incidents end to end through a documented API or MCP connection — no dashboard in the loop

citations.quote: You can use the FireHydrant API to configure integrations, define incidents, and set up webhooks--anything you can do on the FireHydrant UI.
An MCP server for interacting with FireHydrant's API.
An API key can perform actions like any other user
FireHydrant supports bot tokens to act on behalf of a computer instead of a user's account.
